question: Can DDPMs reach competitive log-likelihoods, sample with far fewer steps, cover the data distribution better than GANs, and scale with compute?
hypothesis: Learning the reverse-process variances, a better noise schedule and a hybrid objective improve log-likelihood and allow fast sampling without hurting sample quality.
contributions: Learned reverse variances (interpolation between beta_t and tilde-beta_t) with a hybrid objective L_simple + lambda L_vlb
Importance sampling of diffusion step to reduce gradient noise of L_vlb
Sampling with a strided subsequence of steps (50-100 steps instead of 4000)
Scaling of FID and NLL with training compute

method.summary: A UNet DDPM trained on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet 64x64 (also LSUN bedroom, ImageNet 256x256) with T=4000 steps, a cosine noise schedule, learned variances Sigma = exp(v log beta + (1-v) log tilde-beta) and L_hybrid = L_simple + 0.001 L_vlb with stop-gradient on the mean. Sampling uses K evenly spaced steps from the training schedule.
method.task: unconditional and class-conditional image generation with diffusion models

datasets.name: ImageNet 64x64
datasets.split: unconditional uses official ImageNet-64; FID reference stats from full training set
datasets.preprocessing: class-conditional 64x64 and 256x256: center crop and area downsample

datasets.name: CIFAR-10
datasets.split: FID reference stats from full training set

models.name: Improved DDPM UNet, ImageNet 64x64, C=128
models.architecture: UNet, four downsampling steps with three residual blocks each, channels [C,2C,3C,4C], multi-head attention (4 heads) at 16x16 and 8x8, timestep conditioning GroupNorm(h)(w+1)+b

models.name: Improved DDPM UNet, CIFAR-10
models.architecture: UNet, three resblocks per downsampling stage, widths [C,2C,2C,2C], C=128

models.name: Class-conditional small
models.architecture: class embedding added to timestep embedding

training.objective: L_hybrid = L_simple + lambda L_vlb, lambda = 0.001, stop-gradient on mu output in L_vlb term; L_vlb with importance sampling p_t proportional to sqrt(E[L_t^2]) as an ablation
training.lr: 10^-4 (scaled by 1/sqrt(channel multiplier) for scaling runs; LSUN also 2e-5 at batch 64)
training.batch_size: 128 for most experiments; 2048 for larger class-conditional ImageNet 64x64; 64 or 128 for LSUN
training.dropout: CIFAR-10 swept {0.1,0.2,0.3}: 0.1 best for linear, 0.3 for cosine; ImageNet 64 dropout 0 / 0.1 / 0.3 tried in sweep
training.regularisation: EMA over parameters rate 0.9999; early stopping because of overfitting on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet 64
training.compute: theoretical FLOPs on x-axis of Fig 10 (1e17 to 1e20), assumes full hardware utilization
training.wall_clock: sampling a single image takes several minutes on a modern GPU with 4000 steps

other.cosine_schedule: alpha_bar_t = f(t)/f(0), f(t)=cos^2(((t/T+s)/(1+s)) pi/2), s=0.008, beta_t clipped to 0.999
other.importance_sampling_history: previous 10 values per loss term, uniform sampling until 10 draws for every t

inference.decoding: ancestral sampling over a strided subsequence of K steps: K evenly spaced reals in [1,T] rounded to nearest integer; Sigma rescaled automatically
inference.samples: FID from 50K samples, except unconditional ImageNet 64x64 which uses 10K (biases FID higher; 50K lowers FID about 2 points)

parameters.ddim_stride: constant stride with final timestep T - T/K + 1

metrics.name: Precision / Recall
metrics.definition: Kynkaanniemi et al. 2019 improved precision and recall, Inception-V3 features, K=5

eval.protocol: single runs reported; no seeds or confidence intervals stated

limits: Scaling results are called preliminary; NLL does not fit a power law cleanly.
Models overfit on CIFAR-10 and class-conditional ImageNet 64x64; early stopping needed.
Unconditional ImageNet 64x64 FID uses 10K samples, biasing FID higher by about 2 points relative to 50K.
Likelihood is worse than fully transformer-based models.
Hardware, seeds and wall-clock for training are not stated; single runs.
BigGAN-deep still beats the small diffusion model on FID and remains better on 256x256 (7.0 vs 12.3).
